result.answer:
根据提供的资料（来源1和2），在常规质量控制中，**MTF在2.5、5和7.5 cycles/mm处相对于基线的最大允许偏差为10%**。

具体依据如下：

- 来源1（第128页）第4.2.11.5节“(b)”明确指出：  
  > “The MTF at 2.5, 5 and 7.5 cycles per millimetre should not differ from the baseline by more than 10%.”  
  （MTF在2.5、5和7.5 cycles/mm处的值与基线的差异不应超过10%。）[1]

- 来源2（同页图像说明）也重复了该条款，并确认其为质量控制中的容忍限值[2]。

- 来源3（第129页）第4.2.11.7节进一步佐证：  
  > “if the MTF at 2.5, 5 and 7.5 cycles per millimetre has changed by 10% or more from previously measured values, consult the manufacturer’s service representative.”  
  （若MTF在上述频率处的变化 ≥10%，应咨询制造商服务代表。）[3]

因此，**最大 allowable deviation（允许偏差）为 ±10%**。

⚠️ 注意：该10%是**相对偏差**（即 |(当前值 − 基线值)| / 基线值 ≤ 10%），而非绝对数值；实际基线值需在设备验收/初装（commissioning）时测定并记录。资料中未提供具体基线数值或单位外的其他限制条件。

4.2.11.5. Baselines and tolerances
The following should be considered:
(a) The spatial frequencies at which the MTF drops to 50% and 20% should not be less than the values specified for the relevant model.
(b) The MTF at 2.5, 5 and 7.5 cycles per millimetre should not differ from the baseline by more than 10%.
(c) The spatial resolution may vary on different regions of the image receptor if it deteriorates. In this case, the measurement should be repeated at several locations on the image. These images shall then be compared to each other.
(d) Higher noise may cause the MTF to vary locally.
(e) When a line pair resolution tool is used to determine the limiting spatial resolution, refer to the manufacturer’s specifications.
(f) For film–screen imaging, the limiting spatial resolution should be better (higher) than 12 line pairs per millimetre.

summary: This page describes quality control procedures for assessing the Modulation Transfer Function (MTF) of X-ray imaging systems. It specifies recording MTF values at 2.5, 5, and 7.5 cycles/mm, noting where MTF drops below 50% and 20%, and establishing baselines during commissioning. Tolerances include ≤10% deviation from baseline at those frequencies, and minimum resolution requirements (e.g., >12 lp/mm for film-screen). Figure 43 shows an X-ray image of the physical MTF test tool—a bar-patterned device—mounted in a QC phantom.

4.2.	 QUALITY CONTROL TESTS FOR MEDICAL PHYSICISTS
4.2.11.6.	 Frequency
The test is repeated annually, and after changes or service to the detector, 
tube or computed radiography plate reader.
4.2.11.7.	 Corrective actions
If the 50% or 20% frequencies for the MTF, either parallel or perpendicular 
to the chest wall, drop below the manufacturer’s specifications or if the MTF at 
2.5, 5 and 7.5 cycles per millimetre has changed by 10% or more from previously 
measured values, consult the manufacturer’s service representative.
When the limiting spatial resolution is less than the desirable value, confirm 
that the system is performing satisfactorily and that processing is acceptable for 
film–screen systems, and check the radiation output. The focal spot size may 
affect the resolution.
4.2.12.	 Ghosting (computed radiography and digital radiography only)

This test evaluates the severity of artefacts caused by previous exposure to 
the detector in all systems except photon counting systems [18].
4.2.12.2.	 Equipment
The equipment required is 45 mm thick PMMA slabs.
